lines.text: Many learners say: Can you give me an advice?
Better: Can you give me some advice?
Advice has no a or an. Use some.
Some! Can you give me some advice?

data.wrong: Can you give me an advice?
data.right: Can you give me some advice?
data.why: Advice has no a or an. Use some.

native.tip: Перед “advice” нет “an”: “Can you give me some advice?”
native.caption: Ты тоже говоришь “Can you give me an advice?” 😅 По-русски можно сказать «один совет», «два совета», поэтому хочется поставить “an.” Но в английском “advice” так не считают. Правильно: “Can you give me some advice?” Послушай Карлоса и повтори! Больше практики — в приложении Lexkite.
native.comment: Ответ: “some.” Перед “advice” не ставят “an.” Скажи вслух: “Can you give me some advice?” Бесплатный тест для практики здесь: {link}

en.tip: Do not use “an” with advice: “Can you give me some advice?”
en.caption: Do you also say “Can you give me an advice?” 😅 In Russian you can count advice like apples, so “an” feels natural. But English does not count advice like that. Correct: “Can you give me some advice?” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
